titleEn: Students take up to 88 standardized tests before high school, but more testing doesn’t improve learning
titleZh: 高中前多达 88 场标准化考试，更多测试却未必带来更好学习
method: Machine reference translation with paragraph alignment; not manually certified.

paragraphs.en: The public K-12 school system in the United States has become pervasively shaped by standardized testing.
paragraphs.zh: 美国的公立K-12学校系统已经普遍受到标准化考试的影响。

paragraphs.en: I began teaching mathematics in 2005, four years after the federal law No Child Left Behind was enacted. This law expanded state testing and tied test results to school performance.
paragraphs.zh: 我从2005年开始教数学，也就是联邦法律《不让一个孩子掉队》颁布四年后，这部法律扩大了州考试的范围，并将考试结果与学校表现挂钩。

paragraphs.en: Most districts changed their curricula to focus more on the content and skills covered on state tests.
paragraphs.zh: 大多数地区改变了他们的课程，更多地关注州考试所涵盖的内容和技能。

paragraphs.en: Many school districts increased their instructional weekly time for English and mathematics, with average increases of 47% for English and 37% for mathematics from 2001 to 2007.
paragraphs.zh: 许多学区增加了英语和数学的每周教学时间，从2001年到2007年，英语平均增加了47%，数学平均增加了37%。

paragraphs.en: To make room for additional time spent on these subjects, 44% of school districts cut time from other subjects or activities, such as the arts.
paragraphs.zh: 为了腾出更多的时间花在这些科目上，44%的学区削减了其他科目或活动的时间，如艺术。

paragraphs.en: A 2026 study of 67 school districts across 38 states found that, before high school, students take a median of 57 state- and district-required assessments.
paragraphs.zh: 2026年对38个州的67个学区进行的一项研究发现，在高中之前，学生参加57个州和地区要求的评估的中位数。

paragraphs.en: A short-lived law with lasting effects
paragraphs.zh: 一个短暂的法律，具有持久的影响

paragraphs.en: No Child Left Behind was replaced by another law, the Every Student Succeeds Act, in 2015.
paragraphs.zh: 2015年，《不让一个孩子掉队》被另一项法律《每个学生成功法》取代。

paragraphs.en: Although the Every Student Succeeds Act aimed to reduce the role of testing in classrooms, standardized tests continue to shape what teachers teach, how they use instructional time and how schools define success.
paragraphs.zh: 尽管《每个学生成功法》旨在减少考试在课堂上的作用，但标准化考试继续影响着教师的教学内容、他们如何使用教学时间以及学校如何定义成功。

paragraphs.en: All U.S. public schools are required to administer standardized tests in reading and math annually to students in grades three through eight and at least once in high school. These tests measure whether students are reading and understanding mathematics at, above or below the average, when compared to other students across the state.
paragraphs.zh: 美国所有公立学校都必须每年对三到八年级的学生进行阅读和数学标准化测试，高中至少要进行一次。这些测试衡量的是，与全州其他学生相比，学生的阅读和数学理解能力是否处于平均水平之上或之下。

paragraphs.en: Students’ scores on these tests can affect schools’ ratings and rankings, and can also determine whether states monitor or take over public school districts that are not performing well.
paragraphs.zh: 学生在这些考试中的成绩会影响学校的评级和排名，也会决定各州是否监控或接管表现不佳的公立学区。

paragraphs.en: Too much time
paragraphs.zh: 太多时间

paragraphs.en: The exact number of tests students take each year before high school ranges from 35 to 88 tests. The study also found no relationship between the number of assessments students took and their proficiency or growth in English or mathematics.
paragraphs.zh: 学生在高中之前每年参加的考试的确切数量从35到88次不等。研究还发现，学生参加的评估数量与他们的英语或数学水平或进步之间没有关系。

paragraphs.en: The National Association of State Boards of Education also reports that some districts give students seven assessments per grade, with most tests administered one to three times a year.
paragraphs.zh: 全国州教育委员会协会还报告说，一些地区给学生每个年级七次评估，大多数测试每年进行一到三次。

paragraphs.en: Older research also documents the time teachers spend preparing students for state tests.
paragraphs.zh: 更早的研究还记录了教师为学生准备州考试所花的时间。

paragraphs.en: A 2016 survey found that 62% of K-12 public school teachers reported spending too much time preparing students for state-mandated tests. Teachers estimated spending an average of 14 out of 180 school days preparing students for these exams, whether it be reviewing the question formats students see on tests or teaching test-taking strategies.
paragraphs.zh: 2016年的一项调查发现，62%的K-12公立学校教师报告说，他们花了太多时间为学生准备国家规定的考试。教师们估计，在180个上学日中，平均有14天花在为学生准备这些考试上，无论是复习学生在考试中看到的问题格式还是教授应试策略。

paragraphs.en: In the same 2016 national survey, 29% of teachers reported spending more than a month preparing students in grades K-12 for state-mandated tests.
paragraphs.zh: 在2016年的全国调查中，29%的教师报告说，他们花了一个多月的时间为K-12年级的学生准备国家规定的考试。

paragraphs.en: Costly in other ways
paragraphs.zh: 在其他方面代价高昂

paragraphs.en: Teachers also feel the effects of spending so much time preparing students for standardized tests.
paragraphs.zh: 老师们也感受到了花这么多时间为学生准备标准化考试的影响。

paragraphs.en: Research on teacher turnover has found that teachers’ dissatisfaction with standardized testing was a key reason they left the profession.
paragraphs.zh: 对教师离职率的研究发现，教师对标准化考试的不满是他们离开这一职业的一个关键原因。

paragraphs.en: Other research from 2026 found that teachers who worried about job consequences tied to test results reported lower job satisfaction.
paragraphs.zh: 2026年的其他研究发现，担心考试结果对工作造成影响的教师工作满意度较低。

paragraphs.en: These numbers tell a larger story. The costs of standardized testing do not simply appear in the amount printed on contracts with testing companies.
paragraphs.zh: 这些数字说明了一个更大的问题：标准化考试的成本并不仅仅体现在与考试公司签订的合同上。

paragraphs.en: They are also reflected in lesson plans, teachers’ workloads, classroom time, professional autonomy and the opportunities that disappear when preparing for a test becomes a central purpose of schooling.
paragraphs.zh: 它们还反映在课程计划、教师的工作量、课堂时间、专业自主权以及当准备考试成为学校教育的中心目的时消失的机会中。

paragraphs.en: A test can measure learning. But when some students take as many as 88 assessments before high school and teachers report spending weeks preparing students for state exams, it’s important to ask whether it’s the best use of their limited time.
paragraphs.zh: 考试可以衡量学生的学习情况。但是，当一些学生在高中入学前参加多达88次考试，而老师们报告说，他们花了数周时间为学生准备州考试时，问一问这是否是对他们有限时间的最佳利用就很重要了。

paragraphs.en: I work in Mississippi, where many communities are rural and agriculture is a major industry. Recently, I lamented to a local farmer about the time and money spent on standardized testing. He offered a simple response: “You don’t get a pig to grow by measuring it more.” His words capture the question at the heart of this debate: Does more testing help students learn, or does it take time away from learning?
paragraphs.zh: 我在密西西比工作，那里的许多社区都是农村，农业是主要产业。最近，我向当地一位农民抱怨在标准化测试上花费的时间和金钱。他给出了一个简单的回答：“你不能通过测量猪来让它成长。”他的话抓住了这场辩论的核心问题：更多的测试是帮助学生学习，还是占用了学习的时间？
